memory_update.text: TreeHouse Foods was the cleanest US-listed private-label food manufacturing reference, but it completed a take-private transaction on February 11, 2026; remove THS from active public-candidate universes and track as a private benchmark only.

SENEA is a low-attention public private-label/value-staples processor candidate with packaged fruits/vegetables, contract packaging, food packaging assets, and agricultural/canning/freezing bottleneck angles.
JBSS is a strong underfollowed candidate for private-brand snack nuts, bars, trail mix, and contract manufacturing; food-safety certification and retailer concentration are key evidence tracks.
MAMA is an adjacent cold-chain prepared-food supplier candidate; require explicit verification of private-label or retailer-specific SKU exposure before upgrading beyond hypothesis.

For this node, customer concentration should be scored as both positive dependency evidence and a major falsification/risk variable because retailer repricing, SKU loss, recalls, or failed audits can quickly impair suppliers.
SENEA should be tracked as a high-relevance underfollowed public private-label/contract-packing food processor for value-tier grocery staples.
ODC is a non-obvious private-label household/pet staples input supplier; verify current store-brand cat litter exposure and retailer concentration.
Cold-chain/frozen-food production and customer-label qualification appear to be a credible sub-node of private-label staples manufacturing; LW is a scaled but less pure example.

Many pure-play private-label household and food manufacturers are private, acquired, or buried inside larger companies; later layers should search SEC filings for customer concentration and private-label terms rather than relying on industry labels.

SENEA is a priority underfollowed candidate for the private-label/value-tier staples contract-manufacturing node because FY2025 disclosures show economically material food-packaging exposure and direct private-label/contract-packing relationships.

JBSS is a priority underfollowed candidate because private-brand bidding, snack/nut/bar manufacturing, and two-customer concentration around roughly half of FY2025 sales create a clear hidden customer-dependency research path.
REYN should be retained as a reference-adjacent household consumables supplier, not the main alpha-hunt target, because it is larger and more visible but has explicit store-brand exposure.

BRID is a speculative shadow candidate only; private-label relevance is explicit, but sub-$300m market cap, likely low liquidity, customer concentration, and possible financial fragility require aggressive falsification before promotion.

TreeHouse Foods would have been an obvious pure-play private-label reference historically, but current search context indicates it was taken private; do not treat THS as a current US-listed candidate without re-verifying listing status.

For later layers, separate true private-label manufacturers from branded food companies with incidental co-pack exposure; the key falsification variables are private-label revenue share, customer concentration, qualification gates, plant utilization, recall history, and gross-margin durability under retailer bidding pressure.

SENEA should be tracked as a direct underfollowed private-label/contract-packaged shelf-stable and frozen food processor; verify customer concentration and private-label growth before promoting beyond Layer 1.

CALM maps to private-label/value-tier staples through egg production, grading, packaging, cold-chain distribution, and specialty/conventional private-label shell eggs; key risk is commodity egg-price and avian-flu cyclicality overwhelming the private-label thesis.

ODC is an adjacent private-label consumer-staples candidate via cat litter and absorbent products; it belongs in an underfollowed lane because the public-market label is specialty minerals rather than consumer private label.

For this node, retailer qualification, packaging formats, cold-chain or shelf-stable processing capacity, and customer-label production history are the key chokepoint variables to verify across candidates.

TreeHouse Foods is a strong historical reference for private-label food manufacturing, but current US-listed status must be verified before inclusion in any investable universe; avoid using it as an active candidate until listing status is confirmed.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the public-company universe for the private-label/value-tier staples manufacturing node. TreeHouse Foods would have been the cleanest public reference name, but it was taken private by Investindustrial on February 11, 2026, creating a public-market coverage gap. The remaining US-listed universe is therefore more fragmented: large retailer customers such as Walmart anchor demand, while underfollowed small/mid-cap manufacturers with private-brand, contract-manufacturing, retailer qualification, food-safety, and customer-concentration exposure include Seneca Foods, John B. Sanfilippo & Son, and Mama's Creations. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Expanded the underfollowed lane around scarce or hard-to-switch private-label/value-tier consumer staples supply. The strongest public-company fits found in this pass are not broad branded CPG leaders, but processors and input suppliers with category-specific plants, customer-label capability, retailer/customer concentration, food-safety or product qualification friction, or raw-material/capacity exposure. TreeHouse Foods appears to be a useful reference case for the node, but current search evidence indicates it was taken private, so it is not included as a candidate. Layer 1B expanded the private-label/value-tier contract-manufacturing node toward US-listed, underfollowed suppliers rather than headline retailers.
